subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: ESG and Supply Chains
description: A short lesson to help you apply ESG and Supply Chains.

hook.text: A company's ESG score drops because a supplier uses child labor. Investors pull $500 million in funds.

buildup.text: ESG—Environmental, Social, and Governance—ratings increasingly evaluate supply chain practices, not just direct ones.

discovery.text: Investors use ESG scores to assess long-term risk. Poor supply chain practices signal hidden liabilities.

twist.text: ESG reporting standards vary widely. What counts as 'good' in one framework may not in another.

climax.text: The convergence of global ESG standards is pushing companies toward consistent supply chain accountability.

punchline.text: Your supply chain is your ESG report. Investors are reading it.

quiz.question: Why do investors care about supply chain ESG performance?
options: Poor practices signal hidden long-term liabilities
